summary_responses.response: Cloud microservices often suffer from overload-induced rejections that disproportionately harm high-priority transactions and can be exploited by attackers via retry storms. The paper introduces DiffTry (Differential Retries), a stateless mechanism that assigns class-specific retry limits to differentiate treatment between priority classes during overload. By granting high-priority requests more retry attempts than low-priority ones, DiffTry reduces their rejection rate to around 15% and increases their goodput to roughly 85% of successful completions, even when both classes contribute equal input load. Theoretical analysis across single services and general networks proves the approach converges, yields unique solutions for DAG topologies, and guarantees monotonic improvement in class-level success rates as retry limits increase. Validation on a live Kubernetes deployment confirms that rejection rates closely match the analysis, and DiffTry functions as a drop-in service-mesh plugin requiring no application-code changes.
